quests.title: GAYA
quests.allDone:
Hiro is asleep four feet away and he is taller than you have ever been, and the sword his father drowned holding is across his knees where he put it down.

Michelle went home. The wood went back into its own three nights and took the whole clearing with it. Yugga is four streets away on purpose, which is the only thing left that he could do and the first thing he has done in nine years.

You have no stone. A man has it, and he asked you for nothing, and he called that a wish.

Gaya is where you left it. Go home.

steps.text: LET, at the town gate — nothing armed walks into this town
why: THE GATE
The warden has the only strongbox on Gaya and your name is on the label. You get a racket for it.

steps.text: VESPER, at the church — they have dreamt about you nine nights
why: THE FIRST VOICE
Every fox under that roof has had the same dream, and one of them has been waiting for your face to be in the room.

steps.text: GRISH, in the square — the Open is a player short
why: THE OPEN
He is a Hero of Gaya and he is asking you, which tells you how short they are.

steps.text: FAULT, at the stadium — nobody on Gaya has ever scored a point
why: THE STADIUM
Hit one back at him. They have played this for a century without ever counting it.

steps.text: SLICE, first round of the Open — the church pays the winner in robes
why: FIRST ROUND
Low and flat and she does not let it sit up. The white comes off this match however it ends.

steps.text: THE SACRED WHITE — the mountain road is church ground and it checks
why: WEAR IT
Owning the robe is not wearing the robe. The road up is shut to anything else. Switch it in the weapons menu.

steps.text: CHALK, in the mountain cave — she knows what the vein is doing
why: THE DEEP CUT
The fox at the face is the only one who will say what the vein is doing — and the only one who knows what is sitting on the last whole stone.

steps.text: THE GLASS, over the gorge — look through it and see what they see
why: THE GORGE
Four hundred years of looking at the same world through the same stone. Stand at the plinth and look.

steps.text: VESPER, at the church — tell him what to do about the vein
why: SEAL IT OR CUT IT
Eleven foxes work that face. He has asked you and he means to do whatever you say.

steps.text: THE PAINTED GIANT, in the deep cut — it is standing on something
why: THE GIANT
Five hundred hit points, and one whole uncut stone on the floor underneath it.

steps.text: VESPER, at the church — he will walk up to the gorge with you
why: WALK WITH ME
He will not take the stone off you. He wants to sit down on the platform and find out what the dream was.

steps.text: THE PLATFORM, over the gorge — sit down with him and go under
why: THE PLATFORM
Both of you on the mats, and stay on them. The braziers come up and then the world does not.

steps.text: VESPER, on the platform — tell him what you saw
why: HE IS STILL SITTING THERE
You have been gone about a minute and he has not moved. He has waited nine nights to be told this.

steps.text: GRANT, at the castle — the Steward has to hear what burned
why: THE CASTLE
A fox reached into another world and moved something in it, and then watched that world be hit. Somebody has to be told.

steps.text: RILL, at the great pool — she will ask you once
why: THE SACRED BATH
Guarded every day of the year because it is used one of them. The priest of the water decides when that day is.

steps.text: THE WATER — walk into it, and do not stop at the edge
why: GO IN
Nobody who stops at the edge goes anywhere. The way in is the south side, where the step is.

steps.text: CLAUDE, at the fire — the head of this wood has never met you
why: THE CLEARING
Foxes in the order’s own robe, three hundred years early, getting ready for a wedding.

steps.text: THE CHEST, at Claude’s elbow — a robe, a stone and a fan
why: DRESSED FOR IT
You have come to a wedding in a bath towel. The stone is the one that matters: everybody here is wearing one.

steps.text: CLAUDE, back at the fire — he has a job for you
why: THE WATCH
The path south goes down through the trees to a beach and a dock. Whatever comes, comes up that.

steps.text: THE DOCK — down the path, between them, and out onto it
why: THE TREELINE
Two columns of the wood are standing along that path and none of them will tell you why. Something is on the water.

steps.text: CLAUDE — with the boy, and he will not want to hear it
why: THE BOY
Two dead on the planks, a note about a nobleman in red, and a six-year-old holding your sleeve.

steps.text: THE SAGE, in the hut — he has an offer about the boy
why: SOMEWHERE SAFE
Where you are going next is a throne room with a man in red in it. A six-year-old does not walk in there behind you.

steps.text: THE ROOM TO LET, off the south court — who lived in it
why: THE ADDRESS
The apartment on the east side of the south court is going cheap because the two people who paid for it are dead on a dock, and their landlady knew their business.

steps.text: THE CHAMPION, in the road below the clay — and he is the boy’s uncle
why: THE OTHER UNCLE
The biggest man in Kyoto is standing outside his own gate putting his name on paper for anybody who holds it still. One of Hiro’s two uncles is that man. Ask him.

steps.text: THE STABLEMASTER, on the clay — he says who stands on it
why: NINE DAYS OUT
The champion cannot be reached in tournament week and will not be. The man who decides who gets onto his clay is standing on it, and whatever this is, it goes through him.

steps.text: THE GENERAL, in the throne room — the man in red, at last
why: THE MAN IN THE NOTE
Cast, finally: a general of the northern armies, brother to the champion, uncle to the boy. Everything he tells you is true, which is the trouble with him.

steps.text: THE EMPEROR — and he has exactly one sentence for you
why: HE WILL NOT BE DRAWN
Eleven days of men in black on his own mountain pass, four thousand soldiers in his city, and nothing done about it. He is not going to explain that to a wrestler.

steps.text: THE EMPRESS — the hideout is her file, and so are you
why: SHE HAS THE PATROL REPORTS
She named the men on the pass before anybody asked her to, and she has the only account of how they got up there. Watch what she looks at while she tells you.

steps.text: DESTROY NINJAS AT THE MOUNTAIN CAVE
why: THE CAVE EAST OF TOWN
Farmers with weapons under the straw went up there and did not come down. Somewhere behind them is a family nobody can afford to rush at.

steps.text: THE GIRL WITH THE TRAY — nobody there has ever looked at her
why: WHAT THEY ARE FOR
She has carried tea into that alcove four hundred times and has heard all of it: what happens when the emperor dies, and what the Empress has asked the general to find her.

steps.text: THE WAR CHEST — whoever pays them writes to them
why: THE BACK OF THE CAVE
The big man at the back is wearing the key. What is in the box is worth more than what is in the box.

steps.text: THE EMPEROR — a thing you can put on a table
why: THE PAPER HE ASKED FOR
He told you this court does not believe a man, it believes a thing you can put on a table. You are carrying one.

steps.text: THE THRONE ROOM — with the boy, or without him. Your call.
why: THE ONLY ONE THAT IS YOURS
His uncle asked you to bring him and every word the man said was true. To do it you have to go up the mountain, take him off the sage, and walk him down here past four chances to turn round.

steps.text: THE THRONE ROOM — somebody has to stand in front of that chair
why: PROTECT THE EMPEROR
Takeshi has come down off the dais and told the guards to take his father. The big man at the emperor’s right hand is one man.

steps.text: THE SQUARE — the light came down and it did not come for you
why: IN FRONT OF EVERYBODY
It took him off a crowded street in daylight and the whole city watched. Go and say so — to the old man, and then to her.

steps.text: THE WOOD, south of the square — ask what came down
why: ONE OF YOURS
The Head of the Wood is a thousand years old and he felt it from the clearing. He knows what she is because he is the same thing, and so are you.

steps.text: THE TOP OF THE CAVE — the roof is down and she is behind it
why: SHE DID NOT RUN
Up the mountain road, into the hideout, and through the fall in the corridor. Both feet, hard, more than once.

steps.text: THE STABLE — the board came down to one name, and it is yours
why: THE FINAL
Nine years and nobody has taken a step off him. The stablemaster will put you on the clay with him the moment you ask.

steps.text: YUGGA — the boy’s last uncle, and the only one still standing
why: ASK HIM
He has known Hiro was alive for nine years and done nothing about it for nine years. Tell him where the boy is and he will walk out of his own tournament.

steps.text: THE PLATFORM — four of you, and nothing anybody can hit
why: LET HER ASK

She wants the way through and you are the only person on this mountain who has ever been through one. Claude said it in the clearing: nothing you say will work, and she will want something from you within a minute of seeing what you are.

steps.text: THE ROOM — four doors east of the court. Take him home
why: KEEP HIM UNTIL HE CAN HOLD IT
The wood cannot stay and you are already here. Walk him down the mountain and through your own door.

npcs.name: Sounding

lines.text: You keep this glass?
I clean it, I point it, and I write down what people say when they stand up from it.
That last part is the job. The rest is housekeeping.

topics.label: What is anyone supposed to see?
replies: The gorge. That is what it is aimed at and that is what it shows, and on a clear day you can count the falls on the far wall.
Unless you are carrying live crystal. Then it shows the other thing.
I do not describe the other thing. The ones who are told first only ever see what they were told, and then they write it in my book and my book is worth less.

topics.label: How many have looked?
replies: Nine hundred and four, since the book was started. I have taken two hundred and eleven of those myself.
Most of them say nothing at all. Some cry. Two have laughed, and I have both of those written down with the date, because I have wondered about them ever since.

topics.label: Why does it need a crystal?
replies: It does not. YOU do.
The glass is a magnifier. It magnifies. The crystal is the eye — and the one in this plinth has been the order’s eye for four hundred years. Put yours to it and stop asking me.

topics.label: It was green.
replies: Yes.
Write it in the book on your way out. Nine hundred and five entries now, and the word green is in eight hundred of them.
I stopped finding that reassuring some years ago and I have not worked out what I find it instead.

topics.label: Thank you.
replies: Mind the bridge going back. It is perfectly safe and nobody has ever believed me.

npcs.greeting: Put your eyes to the glass. Everyone should see it once.
npcs.bio: Acolyte of the Church of Gaya. Past the novitiate. Trusted with a shrine of their own.

lines.text: Sit down, sit down — no. No, I do not know you.
I know every fox on this earth. I know the ones in the north who will not come south and I know the two on the island who think nobody knows about them. I do not know you.
I am not from here.
No. And you are the SECOND to say that to me this month, which is two more than the thousand years before it.

npcs.bio: A thousand years old and ten tails, which is as many as there are. Knows the name of every fox on this world and has just met one he has never heard of.

npcs.name: Sedge

topics.label: A long way away.
replies: Everybody says that. My mother is from a long way away and it is four hours’ walk.

topics.label: Congratulations.
replies: Thank you. — Ash still does not know I have counted the cups and I would like it kept that way.

npcs.bio: Getting married in three nights and counting cups.

npcs.name: Ash

lines.text: There are nine cups. I have known there are nine cups since Tuesday.

topics.label: You just turned into a light.
replies: I do that when I am nervous. Everybody does that when they are nervous.
You do not? — What do you do?

topics.label: I will not say anything.
replies: You are all right, you are.

npcs.bio: Knows about the cups.

npcs.role: Four hundred years on that stone

lines.text: You are the one Claude does not know. Word gets round a clearing this size in about a minute.
I do not know you either, and it does not trouble me, which is the difference between us.

topics.label: Do men often come?
replies: They come through. They are not looking for us; they are going somewhere and the wood is in the way.
But a wedding is loud and a fire is bright, and a thing you are not looking for is still a thing you find.

topics.label: What happens if they find you?
replies: Nothing, usually. We are a great deal quicker than they are and there is a lot of wood.
Usually.

topics.label: Nothing.
replies: Sit down if you like. The stone is warm.

npcs.bio: Has sat on that stone for longer than anybody has been counting. Four tails, and touchy about it.

npcs.name: Grant

lines.text: You seem very calm tonight, Grant.
Why should I not be? Gaya's fleet is average. Our shields are standard. Our weapons are precisely balanced.
Not the strongest, not the weakest. The middle is comfortable.
Why is Gaya so suspicious of Meru?
Because nothing should be perfectly central. Meru holds the sun, the broken gate, and the network.
One person holds every string. The rest become puppets.

topics.label: The church is cutting your mountain.
replies: The church is cutting the CHURCH’S mountain. That was settled before my grandmother and it was settled in writing.
And it pays for a fleet that is precisely average, which is the only thing that has ever stopped anybody bothering us.
You want me to have an opinion about it. I am very good at not having one, and it has worked for eleven years.

topics.label: Two cutters are dead.
replies: Three. The third was last night and Vesper has not put it in a letter yet.
I know exactly what it costs and exactly what it earns, and I have both numbers on this desk, and I have not been able to make them argue with each other properly.
That is not indecision. It is what balance actually feels like from the inside, and it is horrible, and I recommend it.

topics.label: Nothing, sir.
replies: Then walk in the square. It is a good square. It is the most average square in the galaxy and I am fond of it.

npcs.bio: Rules Gaya, and is proud of being precisely average at it. Perfectly balanced fleet, standard shields — by design.

npcs.name: Grish

lines.text: Have your explorers found any clues about the 10th Gate?
Not yet. But we track deep-space anomalies on the rim. Some call it the Earth Gate.
A world where our ancestors turned to pure light. I would spend a whole Colony Ship to find it.
Are you ready to back the Player if Luxor attacks?
You bet your tail I am! Grant wants balance. My Fighter hull is already primed.
If Lox starts a fight, Gaya flies beside you.

topics.label: Where would you look for the tenth gate?
replies: The rim, past the survey line, where the charts stop being charts and start being opinions.
There is an anomaly out there that moves about six degrees a decade, which is either a fault in four hundred years of instruments or it is a thing that is moving.
I have asked for one ship. One. They gave me a licence fee schedule instead.

topics.label: The church says Earth is at the gorge.
replies: I KNOW. I have known for six years and they will not licence a survey.
They will sell you a BALL GAME off the back of it — a very good ball game, I have a frame, I am in the draw — and they will not put a ship in the air to go and look.

And here is the part that keeps me awake: if the boy in the cave is right and it is memory rather than a place, then there is nothing out there to fly to, and I have wanted my whole life to be wrong about something else.

topics.label: Nothing, Grish.
replies: Then drink something. Sorrel keeps the kitchen warm for exactly this sort of conversation.

npcs.bio: Gaya's explorer, and the reason its rim survey keeps overrunning. Would spend a whole Colony Ship on a rumour of the tenth gate.

npcs.name: Grand

lines.text: What did you think of the Player's father, Grand?
He was a good man, and a brilliant Steward. Far too trusting. This galaxy eats fair-minded foxes alive.
Do not make his mistakes, child.
Do you think King Might can keep the peace much longer?
Might is a brilliant old fool, rotting from the inside. He built a beautiful cage, that Sphere of his.
Cages shatter when the beast inside outgrows them. Watch your back.

topics.label: What do you make of the church?
replies: They found a hole in the sky and put a turnstile on it. I have no quarrel at all with the turnstile.
My quarrel is that they call the hole holy, so that nobody is allowed to ask who owns it.
Ask Vesper that to his face sometime. He will agree with you, which is the infuriating thing about him.

topics.label: The mountain is waking.
replies: Then stop cutting it. That is not wisdom, child, that is what you say about a dog.
Everyone up there is looking for a subtle answer because the obvious one costs money. I have watched two governments do this and neither of them enjoyed the ending.

topics.label: Nothing, Grand.
replies: Then sit on the pillar a while. It is the only honest thing on this planet — it does not sell you anything and it does not have a view.

npcs.bio: Gaya's commander, and the sharpest tongue on the planet. Knew the Steward's father and is not sentimental about him.

npcs.name: Master of Arms

lines.text: They say you train the guard.
I train whoever walks in. You included, if you have the stomach for the circle.
What should I be working on?
Four things, and everyone favours the wrong one. ATTACK is what your blade takes off them. DEFENSE is what you shrug off.
SPEED is the one nobody respects — it is your feet, your reach, and how often a blow finds nothing but air where you were.
SMARTS is what your scanner tells you and what a clever fox can talk their way into. Sharp enough and doors open that never open for a big arm.
And which do YOU favour?
The one my opponent has neglected. Step in the circle and I will tell you which of yours that is.

npcs.bio: Thirty years in the circle. Has never once been the strongest fox in it and has never once lost to the fox who was.

npcs.name: Guard Captain

lines.text: Captain.
Steward. You have the look of someone who has been winning fights and has not yet asked why.
Ask. I have opinions and a desk, which is a dangerous pairing.

topics.label: What makes a good soldier?
replies: Not courage. Courage is cheap at the start of a thing and gone by the middle of it.
Habit. The fox who has done the boring part ten thousand times does it right on the one day it matters, and does not have to be brave about it.
Show me a guard who keeps their kit clean when nobody is watching and I will show you someone who will still be standing at dusk.

topics.label: When should you NOT fight?
replies: Almost always. Every fight you take is one you could have walked round, and walking round costs you nothing but pride.
Pride is the most expensive armour in this building. It weighs nothing and it has killed more of my foxes than crystal ever has.
The golems on the mountain do not want anything. You cannot negotiate with a rock. But most of what you will meet out there is not a rock.

topics.label: How do you beat something bigger than you?
replies: You do not beat it. You outlast the part of it that is trying to beat you.
Anything large is slow somewhere — in the turn, in the recovery, in the moment after it commits. Find that, and then be somewhere else during it.
And do not stand where it is looking. That sounds like a joke. It is most of the craft.

topics.label: What is the worst habit you see?
replies: Watching the weapon. Everyone watches the weapon. The weapon goes where the shoulders have already decided it will go.
Second worst: fighting the last fight. You beat something once and you keep swinging the answer to a question nobody asked again.
Third: finishing tired. If you are still swinging when your arm is done, you are just handing them the ending.

topics.label: Should the mountain be shut?
replies: Slate has asked me that four times and I have initialled it four times, and you will have heard about that within ten minutes of meeting him.
He is right. He is entirely right, and if I write "agreed" on it then it is the guard telling a church what to do with its own ground, and that is a fight this town does not survive well.
So I initial it and I wait for somebody who is not in uniform to say it. If that turns out to be you, I will deny this conversation and I will mean the denial.

topics.label: Nothing for now, captain.
replies: Then go and be useful. The door is where you left it.

npcs.bio: Commands the barracks. Has thought about fighting for longer than most of the room has been alive, and would rather nobody had to.

npcs.name: Volley

lines.text: You two have been at this a while.
All month. Nobody in here will play me any more.
You have a steady paw. Five points, and I will not go easy — that is the compliment.

npcs.bio: Has held this table against all comers for a month. Says so, anyway.

npcs.name: Pip

lines.text: Any advice?
Yes. Do not watch the ball, watch their paw — they tell you where it is going.
Take my end. Five points. I could do with the rest.

npcs.bio: Loses to Volley about four games in five and turns up anyway.

npcs.name: Cadence

lines.text: What is this desk?
The Second Book. The First Book is what the visions ARE — Vesper keeps that one, and it is mostly weeping.
The Second is what can be done with them. Four hundred years of foxes standing up from that glass saying "they were hitting a ball with a bat", and somebody has to turn that into a rulebook.

topics.label: You invent games.
replies: We RECOVER them. There is a difference and it is worth about nine hundred credits a licence.
Everything in this room came off that gorge. The long table with the small bat — that is in your own tavern, go and watch it. The one with the hoop. Tennis.
Nebo buys three a year. Ur buys one and then copies it, which we price in.

topics.label: Tennis.
replies: The big one. Grass, a net, a strung frame, and a ball that has to bounce once and may not bounce twice.

A hundred years we have had that one, and we still do not know what they were shouting. The numbers are wrong. Fifteen, thirty, forty — that is not counting, that is a clock, and no one has ever explained it.
So we do not play to points. We play until one of them has had enough, which is at least honest about what we do and do not know.

topics.label: Give me one of these rackets.
replies: Take one. They are not sacred, they are stock. There are ninety in the cupboard and I am judged on how few come back.
Ash frame, gut strings, and the order’s mark on the throat so nobody sells it on as an Ur copy.
It is not a weapon. I want to be entirely clear that it is not a weapon, and that whatever you do with it on that mountain is not the order’s doing.

topics.label: What else is in the book?
replies: Nine we sell. Four we cannot make sense of. One we do not write down.
That last one is two of them standing very still, facing each other, and then one falls over. No ball. No frame. Nothing in either hand.
Vesper says it is a rite. I say it is a game we have not understood yet, and I say it because the alternative is that we have been selling somebody’s religion as an afternoon out.

topics.label: Have you been to the gorge?
replies: Twice. Once at ordination, because you have to, and once because I thought I ought to have another look.
It is not for me. I sat down afterwards for about an hour and then I came back here and did some arithmetic, which is what I am for.
The ones who go up a lot end up like Chalk. Ask them what day it is and they tell you about the light.

topics.label: Nothing for now.
replies: Then mind the shelves. Half of this is older than the Gate and all of it is flammable.

npcs.bio: Writes down what the glass shows and then works out how to sell it. Has never been up the mountain and has no intention of going.

npcs.name: Brace

lines.text: Is this as far as it goes?
For anyone not of the order, yes. Above this platform is church ground.
I am sorry. I would let you past — and then I would be a novice who let somebody past, and that is the whole of what I would be.

topics.label: What is up there?
replies: The face, the cutters’ camp, and the cave under it. And whatever has been coming out of the cave for eleven days.
I have not seen it. I have heard it twice, at night, and both times it was further down the road than the night before.

topics.label: Who can go up?
replies: The order. Cutters under contract. And anyone the First Voice has put in grey.
Go and ask him. He says yes more often than the rule makes him. That is not for me to say out loud, so I have not.

topics.label: Right.
replies: The hut is open below if the weather turns. It is always open.

npcs.bio: Nineteen days a novice and he has been given a road to hold. Takes it extremely seriously, which is the only tool he has.

npcs.name: Quartz

lines.text: You are still working.
The face is still standing. Same thing.
Mind the bridge on your way north. Whatever is coming down does not care about the bridge, and I have already rebuilt it once this month.

topics.label: What changed?
replies: The colour, first. It used to cut white and it cuts blue now, all the way through, which is not a thing crystal does.
Then it started answering. You put a chisel in down here and something two hundred yards up the gallery stands up.
The priests call that waking. We called it a bad seam for about a week, because we wanted to, and then we admitted they had a word for it and we did not.

topics.label: Do you want them to stop cutting?
replies: I want to be paid. Ask me an easier one.
— No. There is no honest version of this where we keep cutting and the road gets safer. I have looked for one. I looked for one for a fortnight.
Vesper knows it too. He is waiting for somebody else to say it out loud so that it is not him that said it. That is not cowardice exactly. It is close enough to be going on with.

topics.label: What is at the bottom?
replies: The vein proper. A face of it the size of this bridge, and it is lit from inside, and it is the most beautiful thing on this planet.
And the boy. He is sat in front of it and he has been sat in front of it for eleven days and he is not raving, he is not starving, and he is not coming up.
Take him a word from me: the seventh prop is out and I am not sending anyone down to fix it. He will know what that means.

topics.label: Right.
replies: Keep left at the mouth. The right-hand gallery is where the heavy ones sleep.

npcs.bio: Twenty-two years on the cut face. Can tell you the exact day the crystal changed, and will, at length, whether or not you asked.

npcs.name: Chalk

lines.text: Chalk. They are looking for you.
I know. I can hear the whole mountain from here, so I can certainly hear Brace counting the days on the platform.
I am not lost, I am not enchanted, and I have not stopped eating. I came down to settle one question and I have most of an answer.

topics.label: What question?
replies: Whether the visions are IN the crystal, or in us.
Four hundred years of the order teaching that the stone is a window onto somewhere else. Nobody has ever asked why a window would only work for foxes.
It is us. It was always going to be us. The crystal is a LENS, and a lens does not get to decide what is on the other side of it.

topics.label: Then what is on the other side?
replies: Memory. Ours. From so far back that we filed it under another world and started charging admission.
That lawn is not somewhere we are going. It is somewhere we have been, and the reason it is always green and never winter is that nobody remembers a place they left in the cold.
Do not take my word for it. Go up to the gorge, put your eye to the order’s own stone, and then tell me you are looking at a stranger.

topics.label: Why is it waking, then?
replies: Because we are cutting the lens.
Every piece the order takes out is a piece it cannot see through any more. It is not angry with us. Nothing up here is angry. It is squinting.
The heavy ones on the road are what squinting looks like from underneath. I am sorry about the cutters. I am sorrier than the order is, and I have more of a case to answer.

topics.label: Quartz says the seventh prop is out.
replies: Then the gallery has about a season. He is telling me to come up and he is doing it in the only language he trusts.
Tell him I heard it. Tell him I said the seventh prop has been out since the ninth and I have been sitting under it on purpose.
That will make him furious, which will make him feel better, which is the point of it.

topics.label: Then I need a piece of the face.
replies: Not off me. I have a hammer and no right to use it, and anything I broke off for you would be a shop piece with the life going out of it before you reached the road.
And there is no need, because there is one piece on this mountain that has never been cut. It is on the floor of the deep cut, below this gallery, and there is something sitting on it.
Painted. Taller than the props. It has not moved in eleven days and it does not have to — everything that wakes up on this face walks to it.
That is the stone that takes you under, and it is the only one. Do not go at it with the frame you walked in here holding.

topics.label: I will come back.
replies: You will. Everyone does, once they have looked. Bring the argument with you — I have not had one in eleven days and I am starting to agree with myself.

npcs.bio: Went down to look at the vein properly nineteen days ago and has not come up. Entirely lucid, which is the part that frightens people.

npcs.name: Deuce

lines.text: Is this the Open?
It is. Gaya Open, hundred and first running, and we are two players short because the mountain is eating cutters.
You are carrying a frame. That makes you two players short of one.

topics.label: How does it work?
replies: Three rounds off my sheet. Slice, then Loft, then Ace. You will not beat Ace.
And the rules of a round here are the rules of the circle in the barracks — you go until one of you has had enough. We do not play to points.
The priests never worked out what the numbers meant, so a hundred and one years of this Open have been decided on stamina and bad temper. I have made my peace with it.

topics.label: Who is Ace?
replies: Champion nine years. Came down out of the cutters’ camp on the mountain at fifteen and has never gone back up it.
Takes everything early. If you are waiting for it to come to you, the point is already over and you are still deciding.

topics.label: Who pays for all this?
replies: The church, and the buyers in the box are here to watch the product rather than the players.
Ledger up there has bought two games this week and has not clapped once. Not once. I have been counting, which tells you how the week has gone.

topics.label: Where do the games come from?
replies: The gorge. Everyone knows that and nobody says it inside the ground, because the moment you say it out loud somebody asks whether we are playing a rite.
I have called eleven hundred matches. Whatever it is, it is a game by now. That is what a hundred years does to a thing.

topics.label: Nothing.
replies: Then sit down. Or do not — there are three thousand foxes in here and not one of them is sitting.

npcs.bio: Calls the Open, keeps the book, and has never once been thanked by anybody on either side of the net.

npcs.name: Slice

lines.text: You are in the draw?
First round. Which means I am whoever they found, and this year they found you as well.
Low and fast, and I do not lift it. If you are waiting for it to come up, it will not.

topics.label: What is the trick?
replies: There is no trick, there is a habit. I hit the same shot four thousand times last winter in a barn.
Everyone in this draw has one shot. The difference is whether you have admitted which one it is.

topics.label: Nothing, good luck.
replies: To you as well. Briefly.

npcs.bio: Plays everything low and fast and has never in her life hit a ball above the height of the net. It works far more often than it has any right to.

npcs.name: Loft

lines.text: Second round?
Every year. Second round, semi twice, final twice, and one of those was close.
Beat Slice first. I am not warming up for somebody who is going out in an hour.

topics.label: Two finals?
replies: Two. Nine years ago and six years ago, both against Ace, both of them long.
People ask whether I mind. I have played the best player on this planet twice in a final and I would like to do it again, so no, I do not mind, I am just slow.

topics.label: Nothing.
replies: Go and win a round, then.

npcs.bio: Puts everything up. Has lost two finals to Ace and describes both of them, accurately, as close.

npcs.name: Ace

lines.text: They say you do not lose.
They say a lot in here. Beat the two in front of me and then say it to my face and we will see what it is worth.

topics.label: You came off the mountain?
replies: My father cut for the order. I carried water up that road until I was fifteen and I have not been up it since.
They gave me a frame because there was one spare in the cupboard. That is the entire story and everybody wants it to be longer.

topics.label: Nothing.
replies: Then stand somewhere else. I am working.

npcs.bio: Champion nine years running. Came out of the cutters’ camp at fifteen with a borrowed frame and has not lost a final since. Does not talk about the mountain.

npcs.name: Ledger

lines.text: You are not from here.
I am from wherever the last licence was signed. This week that is here, and next week it is not.
I have taken two of theirs already. I will take a third if the frame game holds up under a crowd that has not been told what to shout.

topics.label: What makes a game worth buying?
replies: It has to be losable. Nobody has ever paid to watch a thing that anybody could do.
And it has to survive translation. Half of what this church sells is a rite with the religion filed off, and the ones that travel are the ones where the filing left something behind.
Tennis has a net. A net is an argument you can see from the back row, and that is worth more than every scripture in that library.

topics.label: Do you know where they come from?
replies: I know what they tell buyers. A gorge, a glass, and a world called Earth that we are all supposedly from.
I do not care whether it is true. I care that nobody else has one, and that the price holds while nobody else has one.

topics.label: I have looked through the glass.
replies: Have you. Then answer me one thing, and do not think about it first.
Was it green?
You did not even pause. That is three of you who have said green to me, on three different worlds, and not one of you had ever met the other two.
I am going to buy the third game. And I am going to stop asking that question, because I do not care for where the arithmetic on it goes.

topics.label: Nothing.
replies: Then move along the rail. You are in front of the umpire and he is already having a week.

npcs.bio: Buys games for a living. Has been in the box since Tuesday and has applauded once, at a line call, and it was sarcastic.

npcs.name: Fault

lines.text: Hoy. HOY. You with the frame — no, you have not got a frame, that is the whole point.
I was only looking.
Everyone is only looking. Deuce is two players short, the draw is on the board, and I have spent the morning counting balls instead of finding him one.
Forty-one. There should be forty-eight. Take this.

topics.label: What is it?
replies: A frame. Ash, gut, church mark on the throat, out of the cupboard nobody counts.
Cadence signs ninety of them out a season and is judged on how few come back, which is why he has stopped counting and I have started.
Hold it like you mean it and nobody in this ground will ask you a single question.

topics.label: I have never played.
replies: Nobody here has PLAYED. We have all done the thing the priests wrote down, which is not the same and everybody knows it.
Grass. Net. It has to bounce once and it may not bounce twice. That is the whole of it and the rest is arguing.

topics.label: Then hit one at me.
replies: Now you are talking. Baseline, that end. I serve.
And do not thank me if you win, I am a ballfox, I am not the standard.

topics.label: Not today.
replies: Suit yourself. I will be here, being seven balls short, until somebody stops me.

npcs.bio: Responsible for forty-eight balls. Has, at any given moment, forty-one balls.

npcs.name: Slate

lines.text: Sergeant.
You are the one they are sending up. Good — then you can carry something down for me.
Twelve guards on that road and not one of them is permitted above the platform, because above the platform is a church. I have foxes holding a line they are not allowed to stand on.

topics.label: So go up anyway.
replies: The order’s ground is the order’s ground, and my captain likes a quiet desk, and both of those are true and only one of them is a reason.
I have put it in writing four times. It comes back initialled. Initialled is not a no. It is a no that does not want to be quoted.

topics.label: What would you do?
replies: Shut the face. Wall the cave. Post four foxes and a bell and let the mountain go back to sleep.
It costs Gaya a fortune. I am a sergeant — fortunes are not my department, and the two cutters were.

topics.label: What is coming down?
replies: Crabs, mostly, and they are quick and they are stupid and we can hold them.
And then the heavy ones, twice, at night. Those we did not hold. We stood aside and let them go past and then went and looked at what they had walked through.
Do not fight one in the open on that road. There is nowhere to go sideways.

topics.label: Nothing, sergeant.
replies: Then arm yourself properly on the way out. The rack is behind me and I am not watching it closely.

npcs.bio: Wants the mountain shut. Has written it down four times and had it come back initialled and unchanged four times.

npcs.name: Let

lines.text: No WEAPONS on the planet. Take this Tennis Racket, it will be all you need, AND if anything shoots at you, hit it back at the sender with the racket.
I expect these weapons back when I go!

npcs.bio: Takes the arms off everybody who lands and has never once been thanked for it. Keeps a written list. The list is his life.

npcs.name: Grish

lines.text: You came. Deuce has you in the book, which means you are in the Open, which means I have my draw.

topics.label: Who do I play first?
replies: Whoever is standing still. Slice, then Loft, and then me if you get that far, and then Ace if you get past me.
Nobody has got past me and then past Ace in the same afternoon. Nobody has needed to. You might.

topics.label: Nothing.
replies: Go and warm up.

npcs.bio: Hero of Gaya, and the reason there is a draw at all this year. Runs the Open, plays in the Open, and has never once seen a problem with that.

npcs.name: the sage of the mountain

lines.text: Come in. Sit by the fire, or do not; it is your fire as much as mine while you are in the room.
— Ah.
You are not a man.
I am standing right here.
You are standing right there and you are a fox, and you are very good at it, and I am old.
Do not do that face. I am not going to shout. I have met four of you and none of them ever did me any harm worth the telling.

topics.label: How did you know?
replies: You hold still to keep it. A man does not hold still to be a man; he simply is one, badly, all day long.
And you look at the door when the fire moves. Foxes do that. It is the only thing about you that is not perfect.

topics.label: Will anyone else see it?
replies: Children. Drunks. Dogs, obviously, and I would keep away from dogs.
And anybody who has ever been robbed by one of you, and that is more people than you would think.
The rest will see a quiet man with a very straight back.

topics.label: I have a child with me.
replies: I know. He is asleep on my step, which is where anybody that tired ends up.
Somebody wants him and has paid men in black to be unpleasant about it, and somebody else wrote it down and did not sign it. Those are usually the same person.
Do not take him to the castle first. Find out who is wearing red before you put a boy in a room with him.

topics.label: Any advice?
replies: Yes, and you will not like it: go slowly. You are a great deal older than this city and you keep behaving as though you were late.
And when it goes wrong — it will — do not be a fox at them. Be a fox somewhere they cannot see, and be a man where they can.

topics.label: Nothing.
replies: Then have some tea and say nothing.

topics.label: What will they make of this sword?
replies: Trouble, is what they will make of it.
You are going down there as a rikishi, which is the only shape in Kyoto that nobody questions — and you are going to hang a samurai’s blade on it.
A wrestler fights with his hands. Every man in armour who sees that sword will want to know which of the two things you are lying about.
Take it anyway. It is the boy’s, and one day he will be big enough to be asked for it back.

npcs.bio: Has lived up here long enough to have stopped being surprised by anything, which is not the same as not noticing.

npcs.name: the landlady

lines.text: You will want the room. Everybody wants the room; nobody wants to say why it is going.
Why is it going?
Because they have not come back, and a month is a month.
Him, her, and the boy. Went down to the coast to meet a boat and that is the end of what I know.

topics.label: The boy is called what?
replies: Hiro. Six, and too polite, which his mother did to him on purpose.
He is the only one of the three I miss, and I am not going to be sentimental about it in front of a wrestler.

topics.label: Has he any family left?
replies: Two uncles, and they are the two ends of this city.
One of them you could not get near with a letter of introduction and a ladder: he is the champion, and he is nine days off the tournament.
And one of them wears red at the castle, and I will say nothing further about that one in my own doorway.

topics.label: Nothing further?
replies: I have three rooms and no husband. Work it out.
He came here twice this year asking after the boy, and both times he was very pleasant, and both times I locked the door after him.

topics.label: Can I take the room?
replies: You cannot, and I am almost glad, because the answer is a good one.
It went yesterday. Bought outright by the man with the counter across the square — the one who cuts the fish and talks while he does it.

He is not letting it to anybody. He says the next person who comes to work for him is going to need somewhere to sleep, and that a man who sleeps four doors from his own counter is a man who turns up.

topics.label: The room again.
replies: Still his. Still empty. Still waiting for whoever is fool enough to stand behind that counter.

npcs.name: the general in red

lines.text: A sumo wrestler. With a samurai’s sword on him. In tournament week.
You are an odd one. Why are you here?

topics.label: Who is the new Empress?
replies: The Empress. Watch how you say it.
She came out of the western provinces a year ago with no family and no province and the emperor has not had an idea of his own since.
I am not complaining. Some of us have waited a long time for this court to grow teeth.

topics.label: I have found your nephew.
replies: — Say that again.
Where. No. Bring him. Bring him to me here and you will not want for anything in this country again.
He is the last of my brother. Whatever you have been paid to bring him this far, I will treble it.

topics.label: Nothing. A wrestler’s question.
replies: Then go and win, and come back when you have.

topics.label: Here he is.
replies: There. There he is.
Hiro. Look at me. — He has his mother's whole face, does he not. The whole of it.
You will be looked after here. Go with the woman; she will show you where you sleep.
And you. Whatever you were paid — name it, and then name it again, because I am not a small man about this.

topics.label: He is not coming.
replies: Say that again.
— You are a wrestler nobody in this city has heard of, and you walked into my throne room carrying my brother's son, and you are telling me you are walking out with him.
I will find him. This is my city, I have four thousand men in it, and you have a boy who cannot run very fast.
Get out.

topics.label: Your brother told me not to let her have him.
replies: — Yugga said that to you.
Then he has understood more from a clay circle in nine days than I have from this corridor in nine years, and he has done it without once having to ask anybody anything.
He is also right, and I am not going to stand here and pretend that the man in front of you is a safer pair of hands than she is.
I am going to say that he is a more frightened one. Decide.

topics.label: — You are staring at my back.
replies: Where did you get that sword.
No. Do not talk yet. Turn a little. — There. The mon on the collar of the scabbard.
That blade belonged to my brother. He wore it at his own wedding and I stood behind him while he did it, and I have not seen it in nine years.
So either he handed it to a sumo wrestler, which he would not have done, or he is dead on a beach somewhere and you were there.
Say nothing. I would rather find this out slowly. — Keep it, wrestler. And keep it out of my brother’s sight; he loved that man.

npcs.bio: Commands the northern armies and wears the colour in a room where nobody else is allowed to. Hiro’s uncle, and entirely sincere.

npcs.name: the emperor

lines.text: They let a wrestler in. Good. Somebody in this room should be able to lift something.
We are drawing a line across the north. Did you know that? I did not, until recently.

topics.label: Whose line is it?
replies: Mine. Obviously mine.
It was explained to me and then it was mine. That is how a good idea arrives — you cannot find the door it came in by, because it was always in the room.
— What were we saying?

topics.label: You seem tired.
replies: I sleep enormously. I wake up further along.
Do not repeat that.

topics.label: Majesty.
replies: Yes. Yes. Go and be enormous somewhere.

npcs.bio: Mild for eleven years and, for the last one, not. Sits very still and agrees with whoever spoke last, provided she spoke last.

npcs.name: the new empress

lines.text: Oh, you enormous thing. Come here where I can see you.
Hm.

topics.label: (Look at her properly.)
replies: She is a fox. Not the shape of one — the fact of one, the way you can tell a lie is a lie in a language you do not speak.
And she has seen you see it, and she is delighted, and she has not stopped smiling at the room for a moment.
"Isn't it a relief," she says, to nobody, pleasantly. "Everyone here is so slow."

topics.label: (The thing at her throat.)
replies: A white disc, a ring of gold, and a black letter on it that this country has no use for. An M.
You have seen that mark. Not here. Not on this world and not in this thousand years — on a wall, on a bridge, on people who called it home.
"You know it," she says, and for the first time she is not enjoying herself. "You KNOW it. Say the name."
"Michelle," she says, before you can. "Say it again in six months and see who is left standing when you do."

topics.label: What do you want here?
replies: "Out," she says. "And I have tried. You cannot imagine how I have tried."
"So: not out. Up. If I am going to be stuck in a dream I am going to be the one it is about."
"There is a child coming. Not born — coming. He will not die and he will be wiser than every man who ever sat in that chair, and one day this whole country will do what he says."
"I would very much like to have him before he is anybody at all."

topics.label: Nothing, Majesty.
replies: "Nothing," she says. "How restful you are."

npcs.bio: Arrived a year ago out of provinces that do not appear to have sent her. Wears something at her throat that is not from this country and not from this world.

npcs.name: the master of the butts

lines.text: You have come up the road from the city, so you have walked past this ground twice and looked at it twice.
It is not a shrine. It is a place where men shoot at things. You may put your hands on a bow if you would like to.

topics.label: What is the mark?
replies: Three arrows. Twenty of the thirty and I will call you an archer — and the bow is yours whatever the straw says.
The gold is ten. Then seven, five, three, one, and off the straw is off the straw and I will not pretend otherwise.
The wind is on the flag. It is on the flag before you loose, which means it is a decision and not bad luck.

topics.label: Why would you give a bow away?
replies: Because you are going up that mountain, and I have been on this road eleven years, and there are men in black in the rocks above the switchback.
A man who can only hit what he can reach is a man who has to walk all the way up to them.
— And because you are a rikishi with a samurai’s sword on your back, and I would quite like to see what you are.

topics.label: How do I shoot it?
replies: Hold the string. Do not pull it and let it go in the same breath — take it back to full and STOP there, and you will feel the moment the bow stops arguing with you.
Then hold your breath, and watch the ring. It goes in and out with your heart and there is a moment between two beats where it is smallest. That is the whole of it. Everything else is arithmetic.
And look at the flag before you look at the gold. The distance is not the hard part. It has never once been the hard part.

topics.label: Give me a bow.
replies: Three arrows. Twenty-eight paces. Twenty points and I will call it shooting — but the bow is yours either way, because there are men in the rocks above that switchback and I am not sending you up there empty.
Nobody shoots against you. There is no honour in it and there is no money in it and the straw does not care who you are. It is you and the mark and whatever the wind is doing.
Hold the string to draw. Hold your breath to steady it. Let go of the string to shoot. Everything between those is the part I cannot do for you.

topics.label: Another time.
replies: The butts will be here. So will I.

npcs.bio: Teaches the bow on the mountain road. Has watched about four thousand people find out that the distance is not the hard part.

lines.text: You are the wrestler with the sword. Do not bother answering; there is one of you.
The general in red has a question he will not ask you out loud, so I have been sent to ask it with this.

Draw it. I will not kill you and you will not kill me — there are forty men through that door and every one of them can count.

topics.label: It was given to me.

Guard up, rikishi.

I have to go. — Good luck, big man.

topics.label: Nothing. An autograph.
replies: There. Hold it by the corner, the ink is wet.

npcs.name: the man at the gate

lines.text: The board is full.
You have not looked at it.

topics.label: Put my name on it.
replies: Names on this plank are men this city has heard of. I have not heard of you and I hear everything, it is the job.
So: through the gate. The stablemaster is on the clay and he will tell you no as well, and he will keep telling you no right up until you have put his whole stable on its back.
Do that, and come out here and say it to me again, and I will find a nail.

topics.label: What is the board?
replies: Sixteen names, a plank, and a month. Two bouts a day until there is one of them left, and then that one goes on the clay with the champion and finds out what he is.
It has been the same name at the bottom of it for nine years, which is either the best thing about this country or the worst, and I am too tired to decide.

topics.label: Nothing.
replies: Then stand somewhere else. You are the size of a door.

Three masks and one man behind all three. It is the oldest thing we do and it still fills the house.

topics.label: Nice mask.
replies: This? Paper and rabbit glue. Forty years old and I have reglued the left ear twice.
The trick is the eyes. Cut them too round and it is a dog. Cut them right and people cross the street.
Yours is very good, by the way. I cannot see the join at all.

npcs.name: the abbot

lines.text: A rikishi’s shoulders, a fox’s manners and a samurai’s sword. You are three things and I do not much mind which.
I want to use the hot spring.
Everybody wants to use the hot spring. The water was ours before there was a city on top of it, so the door is ours, and I give the word.
I do not give it for money and I will not give it for that sword. I give it for an afternoon’s work.
There are six scrolls in the library across the square, one to a row. Read all six. Then answer me this.
I am given one at a time, one for every hundred years, and at nine I am finished. I am not a coat, and I am not a crown. What am I?

topics.label: Which scroll has the answer in it?
replies: I am not going to tell you that.
If I told you which shelf it was on you would read one scroll and learn one thing. Read six and you will not be able to help yourself.

topics.label: Can I not just answer now?
replies: You can answer when you have read them.
A man who guesses at me and happens to be right has told me nothing about himself except that he guesses.

topics.label: Where is the library?
replies: The west arch, under the north wing of the square.
It is the only building in Kyoto with nobody arguing in it. You will know it.

topics.label: Later.

npcs.bio: Keeps the temple, and with it the door to the hot spring.

npcs.name: an old man at a go board

lines.text: Seven lines by seven. Small enough to finish before the tea goes cold, and big enough to lose in.
You are black, so you go first. Surround a stone and it comes off. Surround empty ground and it is yours.

topics.label: Sit down and play.
replies: Black first. Take your time; I have nothing else on.

topics.label: How do I play?
replies: Four rules and one of them is about not going round in circles.
Stones do not move. A group with no empty point beside it comes off the board. You may not put a stone where it could not breathe.
And you may not take a stone straight back the way it took yours. Play somewhere else first. Everything after that is just looking.

topics.label: Any advice?
replies: On a board this size, the corners are worth more than they look and the middle is worth less.
Two eyes and a group cannot be taken. One eye and it is a matter of time.
And if you cannot see a move worth making, pass. Half the game is knowing when there is nothing left to do.

topics.label: Another time.
replies: The board will be here. So will I.

npcs.bio: Has sat on this side of this board every afternoon for fifty years and has never once been seen to win quickly.

npcs.name: the tea master

lines.text: You have come a long way today. I can tell by the way you came through my door.
Sit down. I will make you something.

topics.label: A bowl of tea, please.
replies: A moment. It is not a thing you hurry.

topics.label: What makes it good?
replies: Water off the boil, not on it. Boiling water burns the leaf and then you are drinking the burn.
And the bowl is warmed first, or the first mouthful is colder than the last and the whole thing runs backwards.
That is it. Everything else people tell you about tea is people enjoying telling you about tea.

topics.label: Who is the woman with the fan?
replies: That is Suzu. She has been dancing in this room since before I had the lease on it.
Ask her. She will say no twice and then do it, and you will be glad you asked.

topics.label: Nothing for now.
replies: Then sit anyway. Nobody has ever been thrown out of here for sitting.

npcs.bio: Runs the counter. Has opinions about water temperature that he will share whether or not you have asked for them.

npcs.name: a woman with a fan

lines.text: You are looking at the fan and not at me, which is at least honest.
It is a bad fan. I have better ones. I dance with this one.

topics.label: Would you dance?
replies: No.
I am out of practice and the floor is wrong and it is the middle of the afternoon.
...Sit down, then. Do not clap in the middle.

topics.label: Why that fan?
replies: Because it is light and it is loud. A heavy fan is a beautiful fan and it says nothing when you open it.
The snap is half of it. People think the dance is the arms.

topics.label: How long have you danced?
replies: Long enough that I stopped counting, and then long enough again that I started.
Eleven years in this room. Before that a room in Edo with a lower ceiling and a better floor.

topics.label: Another time.
replies: Good. I did not want to anyway.

npcs.bio: Dances here most afternoons. Says she is out of practice, which is what she has said every afternoon for eleven years.

npcs.name: the sushi chef

lines.text: Any chance you are looking for a job? We got great SUSHI here, super fun to make.

topics.label: Sounds SWEET! Put me to work.
replies: Behind the counter. Rice is warm, the fish is cut, and there are four people waiting.

topics.label: How do I make SUSHI?
replies: Rice first. Everything anybody tells you about fish is people avoiding the rice, and the rice is the whole job.
Warm as a hand, seasoned while it steams, and turned with the edge of the paddle so you never crush a grain.
Then you shape it in three moves and stop. Four moves and it is a ball of rice with a fish on it, and everybody in this room will know.

topics.label: How did you get into the SUSHI business?
replies: My father sold fish off a cart at the north gate and I hated every morning of it.
Then a man came down from the coast and put a counter in a room and stood INSIDE it, and I understood the whole thing in about four seconds.
You are not selling fish. You are standing in the middle of a ring of people having a good evening, and the fish is how you got them to sit down.

topics.label: They say you bought the room across the square.
replies: I did. Ten minutes after the landlady put the notice up, and I have not been inside it once.
It is for whoever works here. Not a favour — I am tired of people who live across the river and arrive at nine with wet feet.
So: stand behind that counter and do a shift, a real one, and the room is yours. Key and all. That is the wage; there is no other one.

topics.label: Put me behind the counter, then.
replies: Rice is warm, the fish is cut, and there are four people waiting.
Do not let me down in front of the carpenter. He notices.

topics.label: I did the shift.
replies: You did. The carpenter says the rice was right, and the carpenter has never said that about anybody.
Here. It sticks in the damp, so lift it as you turn it.
Four doors, east side of the court. Sleep in it. That is what it is for, and I will know if you do not.

topics.label: How is the room?
replies: Yours. I am not asking for it back and I am not asking you to be grateful about it.
Turn up on time and we will never discuss it again.

topics.label: Maybe later.
replies: The sign stays up. Come back hungry.

npcs.bio: Works inside the ring with his back to nobody, which he says is the only way to cook for people.

lines.text: The rice. Everybody says the fish. It is the rice.

npcs.bio: Has eaten here every night for eleven years and never once looked at the board.

npcs.bio: Arguing about somebody who is not here.

lines.text: He puts it down in front of you before you know you wanted it.

npcs.bio: Left the long sword at the door, which is the house rule and he knows it.

npcs.name: a very small boy

lines.text: I am ALLOWED to sit here.

npcs.bio: On a stool that is too tall for him, delighted about it.

npcs.name: the old actor

lines.text: We are a man short and the house is in nine days. Can you stand still?
I can stand still.
Everybody says that. Nobody can.
The play is THE FOX WIFE. A farmer marries a woman who came out of the rain, and does not ask, and then one day he asks. Three masks: the wife, the farmer, the fox.
You wear whichever one the chorus is speaking. The drum tells you when. One rule, and it is harder than it sounds.

topics.label: What is the hard part?
replies: There is only one rule and it is not a difficult one. The chorus names who is speaking. You put that face on, every time.
The hard part is that it does not stop. Twenty-two of them, and the last scene is faster than the first.
And be careful of the changes. A man caught halfway between two masks is not playing anybody, and that is the one thing a house never forgives.

topics.label: What happens if I get it wrong?
replies: Once? Nothing. Somebody coughs.
Again and again and they stop watching the play and start watching the man in it — and there is a bowl of still water on that stage in the third scene.
I have seen a house work out what an actor was. Not often. It is not a thing you come back from in the same evening.

topics.label: Who comes to see it?
replies: Everybody. Which means everybody who matters.
I have played to the man in red four times. He does not laugh and he does not look away, and he watches the wings rather than the stage.
You learn a great deal about a man from where he puts his eyes when he thinks nobody is looking at him.

topics.label: Put me on.
replies: Then take the rack and stand on the mark.
Wear whichever one the chorus is speaking. And when the drum falls, be still.

topics.label: Not tonight.
replies: The house is in nine days.

npcs.bio: Forty years behind a mask, and he can tell you what every face in the house is doing.

npcs.name: a woman who has seen it four times

lines.text: Shh.

npcs.bio: Knows every line and mouths the fox’s.

lines.text: Shh.

npcs.bio: Here because his father is not.

npcs.name: a very old woman

lines.text: Shh.

npcs.bio: Has not blinked since the lamps went down.

lines.text: Shh.

npcs.bio: Fans himself through the quiet parts, which is why nobody sits near him.

npcs.bio: Got in without paying and everybody knows it.

lines.text: I was stood where you are stood. I had my hands in a bucket.
It came down slow. That is the part nobody believes when I tell it — it came down SLOW, like it was being let down on a rope, and it made no noise at all.

topics.label: What did it take?
replies: A boy. Nine, ten. Nobody knew him.
He walked into it. I want that said, because there are three men in this square telling it the other way and I was closer than any of them.

lines.text: Do not ask me in front of her.
She has asked me nine times today whether it comes for everybody’s and I have run out of ways to say no that she believes.

topics.label: It will not come again.
replies: You do not know that.
But say it to her anyway. She will take it off you and she will not take it off me.

lines.text: Four people have asked me this morning whether that was heaven.
I have been ordained two years. I said I would find out, which is not what any of them wanted and is the only honest thing I had.

topics.label: It was not heaven.
replies: No. It was warm and it was low and it was somebody’s.
I am not going to say that from the step. But I am glad to have heard it said.

npcs.name: the new empress

lines.text: “We are not finished. But I am not doing it twice, so go away and come back when you have decided something.”

npcs.bio: Nine years on a world she cannot leave, and a seam at the top of a mountain she cannot open.

npcs.name: Hiro

lines.text: “Go on. I will still be here.”

npcs.bio: The boy off the dock, ten years on, in one room four doors east of the court. He can lift it now.

npcs.name: Plum

lines.text: Busy today?
Every day, near enough. The library reshelves on a Thirdday and the whole avenue queues for it.

npcs.bio: Walks the north avenue most days. Has opinions about the state of the paving.

npcs.name: Mauve

lines.text: Anything I should know?
Mind the crossing. Everyone cuts the corner at the crest and nobody looks.

npcs.bio: Crosses the square four times a day and could not tell you why.

npcs.name: Iris

lines.text: Good morning.
It is, actually. The lilac took at last — third year of trying.

npcs.bio: Grew the lilac in half the window boxes on this street.

npcs.name: Brother Cinnabar

lines.text: Are you of the church?
Of the order, yes. We are not only for the nave. Somebody has to see the town.

npcs.bio: Acolyte of the Church of Gaya. Past the novitiate. Trusted with a shrine of their own.

npcs.name: Amethyst

lines.text: Waiting for something?
A crate. Due on the last ship, and the last ship has been and gone.

npcs.bio: Waiting on a delivery that was due on the last ship.

npcs.name: Lilac

lines.text: You know everyone here.
By their walk, mostly. Faces change. Nobody changes how they cross a square.

npcs.bio: Knows every fox on the square by their walk before their face.

npcs.name: Sister Damson

lines.text: You are a long way from the church.
Sent out to look at it. Hard to pray for a town you have only seen from a window.

npcs.bio: Novice of the Church of Gaya. Newly of the order. Still gets the early bells.

npcs.name: Orchid

lines.text: Keeping well?
Between jobs. Have been for a year. It suits me better than the jobs did.

npcs.bio: Between jobs, cheerfully, for about a year now.

npcs.name: a fishmonger

lines.text: Busy?
Nine days to the tournament. Every stall in this square is praying for a long final and a thirsty crowd.

npcs.bio: Comes up from the coast twice a week and has views on the road.

npcs.name: a woman with a child

lines.text: Long day?
They put the notice up about the northern levy this morning. My husband is thirty-one. He has never held anything sharper than a plane.

npcs.bio: Has a small boy on one hand and a great deal of shopping on the other.

npcs.name: an old man

lines.text: Anything to tell me?
The emperor was a gentle man. I sold him a fan once. Now there are lines being drawn on maps and I am told that is what he always wanted.

npcs.bio: Old enough to remember two emperors and rude enough to compare them.

npcs.name: a carpenter

lines.text: What are you building?
Seats. Whole east side of the playhouse. They open the day after the tournament and I have nine days and one apprentice.

npcs.bio: Rebuilding the theatre’s east gallery and running out of week.

npcs.name: a young priest

lines.text: Are you all right?
People have started asking me whether a war can be a holy one. They never used to ask me anything.

npcs.bio: Walks up from the temple every morning and is not enjoying what he keeps hearing on the way.

npcs.name: a woman selling rice

lines.text: What is the news?
The new Empress. That is the news, every day, all day. They say she has never once been ill and never once sat down.

npcs.bio: Has a stall at the south end and a good ear for the castle.

npcs.name: a tout

lines.text: What are you selling?
Standing room. Day six. Best I can do, and I am doing it for four people already.

npcs.bio: Sells tournament places he does not have to people who cannot count.

npcs.name: a rikishi’s apprentice

lines.text: You are in the stable?
Bottom of it. Nine days out nobody in that house speaks except to say a number. It is the calmest I have ever been.

npcs.bio: Carries the champion’s things and is a very long way from being allowed to say so.

npcs.name: a pilgrim

lines.text: How far are you going?
To the top, and then back down, and then I expect I shall be exactly the same person. That is not a reason not to go.

npcs.bio: Walking to the shrine on the mountain and in no hurry whatsoever.

npcs.name: a monk on his round

lines.text: Are you collecting?
I am walking. If somebody puts something in the bowl that is their business, not mine.

npcs.bio: Walks the square twice a day and takes what he is given.

lines.text: Welcome to Gaya, Steward.
Your ship is fuelled and berthed behind you. The teleporter at the end of the gantry puts you down on the crest pad in town.

topics.label: How do I get back to space?
replies: Walk back to your ship and board her. She will take you up to orbit.

lines.text: Hoy. HOY. You with the frame — no, you have not got a frame, that is the whole point.
I was only looking.
Everyone is only looking. Deuce is two players short, the draw is on the board, and I have spent the morning counting balls instead of finding him one.
Forty-one. There should be forty-eight. Take this.
